# About Kinexus CPAs & Advisors

## Identity
Kinexus CPAs & Advisors is a CPA firm based in St. George, Utah, operating under the tagline "Dedicated Partner for Business Growth & Wealth." The firm describes itself as serving small businesses, entrepreneurs, and individuals with accounting, tax, payroll, and strategic advisory services tailored to each client's industry and stage of growth.

The firm is led by Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, Managing Partner, alongside partners RJ Mathews, CPA; Andrew (Andy) James Stewart, EA; and Katie Bowles, Partner & Operations Manager, who brings 16 years of operations management experience to the firm. The broader team includes Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, Senior Tax Professional with specializations in restaurant and construction industry clients; Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc; Morgan Nethercott, CPA; and Quade Jones, Tax Professionals; plus Candi McMullin (Payroll Specialist), Leslye Haws and Shelby Barlow (Bookkeeping Specialists), and administrative staff (Payton Wilcox, Madi Clark, Paeton Szczepaniak) who support day-to-day client operations.

Contact: info@stgcpas.com | (435) 674-1314 | 216 W St George Blvd, Ste 100, St George, UT 84770. The firm maintains an active Google Business Profile (4.9 rating, 18 reviews) along with LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram company presences.

## Positioning & Differentiation
Kinexus's stated positioning blends year-round proactive tax planning and quarterly projections, deep industry-specific expertise across construction, restaurants, real estate, and medical practices, and CFO-level business management and growth advisory — presenting the firm as a full-spectrum financial partner rather than a compliance vendor.

Differentiators include: industry-specific expertise across construction, restaurants, real estate, medical practices, and service businesses; year-round proactive tax planning and advisory rather than once-a-year tax prep; a modern, secure digital process for document handling and filing; and CFO-level business management services paired with audit protection support.

Ideal clients named by the firm include contractors and construction business owners, restaurant and food & beverage operators, entrepreneurs launching or scaling a business, real estate investors and rental property owners, medical professionals (physicians, dentists, healthcare providers), and service-based businesses such as consultants, agencies, coaches, staffing firms, IT providers, and marketing companies.

Core services supporting this positioning: Outsourced Accounting (bookkeeping, payroll, tax preparation and planning, audit protection); standalone Bookkeeping and Payroll services billed on a fixed monthly fee; Business Tax (strategic tax planning, quarterly projections, business tax return preparation, year-round position management); Personal Income Tax (tiered 1040 preparation across Basic, Deluxe, and Premium levels, audit protection, yearly consultation, estimated payment processing); Audit Protection (representation for IRS notices and audits through appeals or litigation); Business Management Services (CFO-style budgeting, revenue, expense, payroll, COGS, credit card fee, cash flow, and industry KPI analysis); and Business Foundation Services (entity type analysis, accounting system setup, retirement plan analysis, credit card rewards guidance) for entrepreneurs starting a business.

## Industries Served

### Construction
Accounting for contractors and builders covering job costing, certified payroll, cash flow, and tax strategy for a project-based industry.

### Restaurants
Accounting for restaurant and food & beverage businesses focused on food cost tracking, tipped-employee payroll, sales tax compliance, and thin-margin profitability.

### Entrepreneurs
Financial guidance for entrepreneurs at every stage, from entity structure and bookkeeping to cash flow reporting and tax planning.

### Real Estate
Tax and accounting support for real estate investors and property owners, including depreciation, cost segregation, passive loss planning, and 1031 exchanges.

### Medical Professionals
Financial planning and practice accounting for physicians, dentists, and healthcare providers dealing with high tax burdens and practice management complexity.

### Service-Based Businesses
Accounting and advisory for consultants, agencies, coaches, staffing firms, IT providers, and marketing companies built on expertise-driven revenue models.

## Services

### Outsourced accounting
URL: /what-we-do/outsourced-accounting

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: outsourced-accounting-team-meeting.jpg | alt: "Accountant and small business owner reviewing financial reports together at a desk" | query: "accountant business owner reviewing reports" -->
## A dedicated back-office team for your growing business

Most businesses hit the same wall: the bookkeeping has outgrown a part-time solution, but hiring a full-time controller doesn't pencil out yet. That gap is exactly where outsourced accounting fits. Kinexus CPAs & Advisors steps in as your back-office team, handling the day-to-day financial work so you can spend your time running the business instead of chasing invoices and reconciling accounts at 10 p.m.

This isn't tax prep with a bookkeeping add-on. It's ongoing financial management built around your business, staffed by CPAs, EAs, and accounting professionals who track your numbers month over month, not just once a year. St. George business owners in construction, restaurants, real estate, and healthcare use this service to get financial clarity without adding another full-time salary to the payroll.

Think of it as a growth partnership. As your revenue and transaction volume increase, the scope adjusts with you, no renegotiating a new vendor relationship every time you add a location or a crew.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: bookkeeping-reconciliation-documents.jpg | alt: "Financial documents and laptop showing bookkeeping reconciliation records" | query: "bookkeeping financial documents laptop" -->
## What's included in your outsourced accounting package

Every Kinexus outsourced accounting engagement is scoped to your transaction volume and reporting needs, but most packages include the same core building blocks:

- Transaction coding and monthly bookkeeping, categorized to your chart of accounts
- Bank and credit card reconciliations, completed monthly so your books match reality
- Accounts payable management, including bill entry, approval routing, and payment scheduling
- Accounts receivable and invoicing, so cash comes in on time instead of chasing it later
- Monthly or quarterly financial statements: profit and loss, balance sheet, and cash flow reports
- Payroll coordination that ties directly into your books, in step with our [payroll processing](/what-we-do/payroll) team
- A set reporting cadence, so you know exactly when to expect numbers and what they'll tell you

Compare that to a vague promise of "bookkeeping services" and the difference is clear: you know precisely what you're paying for, who's doing it, and when you'll see results. Need bookkeeping alone without the full back-office scope? Our [bookkeeping services](/what-we-do/bookkeeping) can be scaled up or down as your needs change.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Built for the industries driving Southern Utah's economy

Generic accounting advice doesn't hold up against job costing, retainage, or multi-location payroll. Kinexus builds outsourced accounting workflows around the industries that make up Washington County's economy.

### Construction
icon: Hammer

Job costing, WIP schedules, and retainage tracking require accounting that speaks the language of contractors. Our [construction accounting](/who-we-serve/construction) work keeps project profitability visible in real time, not three months after the job closes.

### Restaurants
icon: Receipt

Thin margins and daily cash flow swings mean restaurant owners need current numbers, not stale ones. Our [restaurant accounting](/who-we-serve/restaurants) support covers food and labor cost tracking alongside routine bookkeeping.

### Real Estate Investors
icon: Building2

Rental property owners and portfolio investors need accounting that separates properties, tracks depreciation, and feeds directly into tax strategy. See our [real estate investor services](/who-we-serve/real-estate-investors) for the full picture.

### Medical Professionals
icon: Stethoscope

Physicians, dentists, and healthcare providers deal with insurance reimbursement timing and overhead that outpaces typical small business accounting. Our [medical professional services](/who-we-serve/medical-professionals) address both.

### Service-Based Businesses
icon: Briefcase

Consultants, agencies, coaches, and staffing firms often run lean, so accurate books matter even more when there's no in-house finance department. Our [service-based business](/who-we-serve/service-based-businesses) support fills that role directly.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: secure-digital-accounting-portal.jpg | alt: "Business owner uploading financial documents through a secure online client portal" | query: "secure online portal document upload" -->
## A modern, secure process that saves you time

Paper receipts in a shoebox and spreadsheets emailed back and forth are how bookkeeping used to work. Kinexus runs on cloud-based accounting software and a secure client portal, so documents move digitally from the moment you receive them to the moment they're reconciled.

You upload statements and receipts through an encrypted portal instead of a shared drive with no access controls. Reports arrive on a set schedule instead of "whenever someone gets to it." And because everything lives in the cloud, you can check your numbers from a job site, a restaurant floor, or an exam room without waiting for an email reply.

The payoff isn't just convenience. A secure, digital process protects sensitive financial data and creates a clean audit trail, which matters the moment a lender, bonding company, or the IRS asks for documentation.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: cfo-advisory-strategy-session.jpg | alt: "CPA presenting financial strategy charts to a business owner in an office setting" | query: "CPA presenting financial strategy meeting" -->
## From bookkeeping to CFO-level insight as you grow

Outsourced accounting shouldn't be a service you eventually outgrow and replace. At Kinexus, it's the starting point of a relationship that expands as your business does. What begins as monthly reconciliations and financial statements can grow into full [business management services](/what-we-do/business-management-services): budgeting, forecasting, margin analysis, and the kind of strategic insight normally reserved for a CFO on payroll.

Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, leads advisory work that connects your monthly numbers to decisions about hiring, equipment purchases, and entity structure. RJ Mathews, CPA, and Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, work alongside him on client accounts that span construction, restaurants, and real estate. The result is a single firm that handles your books today and your growth strategy next year, rather than handing you off once tax season ends.

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: accountant-client-handshake-office.jpg | alt: "Business owner and CPA shaking hands after a consultation in a modern office" | query: "business handshake office consultation" -->
## See what a dedicated accounting partner can do for you

If your books are behind, your reports are unreliable, or you're simply tired of doing this yourself at night, it's worth a conversation. Tell us where your business stands and what you're trying to build, and we'll map out what an outsourced accounting engagement would look like for your specific situation, industry, and growth stage.

### Bookkeeping
URL: /what-we-do/bookkeeping

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Bookkeeping built for growing St. George businesses

Ask five local firms what bookkeeping means and you'll get five different answers. For too many, it's a once-a-month data entry task handled by whoever's available, then filed away until tax season. At Kinexus CPAs & Advisors, bookkeeping is the starting point for proactive tax planning, cash flow decisions, and the CFO-level insight that helps St. George business owners grow. Every transaction recorded and every account reconciled feeds directly into the advisory work our CPAs and enrolled agents do year-round, not just in March and April. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and the Kinexus team built this process around a modern, secure digital workflow, so your financials stay accurate, current, and ready to support real decisions. If your books are a mess, or you're outgrowing a solo bookkeeper working out of a spreadsheet, this is where the fix starts.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: bookkeeping-checklist-review.jpg | alt: "Accountant organizing receipts and invoices on a digital tablet" | query: "bookkeeper organizing invoices digital tablet" -->
## What our bookkeeping service includes

Bookkeeping only works if it's consistent, accurate, and built on a system you can actually see into. Our process covers the full back-office cycle:

- Transaction classification and coding, so every dollar lands in the right account
- Expense tracking and categorization for cleaner reporting and easier tax prep
- Bill pay and accounts payable management, so nothing slips past due
- Invoicing and accounts receivable follow-up to keep cash coming in
- Monthly account reconciliation across bank, credit card, and loan accounts

Every client works inside a secure digital portal for document handling and file sharing, not folders of paper receipts or email attachments. That's a different experience than the paper-based, spreadsheet-driven setup many small local bookkeepers still run on. You get real-time visibility into your numbers, a documented audit trail, and a bookkeeping file your CPA can build tax strategy from, because RJ Mathews, CPA, and Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, work from the same clean data you do.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Bookkeeping tailored to your industry

Generic bookkeeping misses the details that matter most to your business. Ours doesn't.

### Construction
icon: Hammer

Job costing, retainage tracking, and work-in-progress schedules require a bookkeeper who understands percentage-of-completion accounting, not just basic expense coding. Project-level costs get tracked as the job progresses, not reconstructed after it's done.

### Restaurants
icon: Receipt

Daily sales reconciliation, tip reporting, food and labor cost percentages, and multi-location tracking need a bookkeeping rhythm built for restaurant margins, not a once-a-month catch-up.

### Real Estate Investors
icon: Home

Rental income, security deposits, property-level profit and loss statements, and depreciation schedules get tracked separately for each property, so you know which assets are actually performing.

### Medical Professionals
icon: Stethoscope

Insurance reimbursement timing, payroll for clinical and administrative staff, and equipment financing all get accounted for with the cash flow patterns specific to a practice.

### Service-Based Businesses
icon: Briefcase

Consultants, agencies, coaches, staffing firms, and IT providers need clean recurring revenue tracking and project-based cost allocation to price services profitably.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: cfo-advisory-meeting.jpg | alt: "CPA and business owner reviewing financial reports together" | query: "cpa business owner reviewing reports" -->
## From bookkeeping to CFO-level insight

Clean books are the beginning, not the destination. Once your bookkeeping is accurate and current, it becomes the data set for real strategy: cash flow forecasting, tax planning that happens across the year instead of one rushed conversation in April, and the kind of business management services that tell you which of your service lines actually makes money. Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, and Morgan Nethercott, CPA, work directly with bookkeeping clients to build that bridge, so a first-time business owner who started with basic transaction tracking can move into CFO-level guidance without switching firms or re-explaining the business from scratch. Your bookkeeper and your tax advisor are the same team, working off the same numbers.

### Payroll
URL: /what-we-do/payroll

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: left-aligned -->
## Payroll built for St. George business owners, not spreadsheets

Payroll sounds simple until a subcontractor gets misclassified, a tipped server's W-2 doesn't match the state filing, or your fifth new hire this quarter throws off your labor budget. Most payroll providers process numbers and move on. Kinexus CPAs & Advisors treats payroll as one piece of a bigger financial picture, reviewed by the same CPAs and Enrolled Agents who prepare your tax return and manage your books.

That matters in St. George, where construction crews, restaurant staff, and medical practice teams all have different pay structures, tax exposure, and compliance risks. You won't get routed to a national call center or left alone in a software portal. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and the Kinexus team run payroll as part of a year-round advisory relationship, not a once-a-pay-period transaction.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: payroll-processing-review.jpg | alt: "Accountant reviewing payroll records and pay stubs at a desk" | query: "accountant reviewing payroll documents office" -->
## What our payroll processing includes

Every payroll run at Kinexus covers the full cycle, not just the paycheck. That includes:

- New employee setup, including I-9 verification, W-4 collection, and direct deposit enrollment
- Salary and wage changes processed the same week they're requested, not batched for next cycle
- Timely, accurate processing on your schedule, whether that's weekly, biweekly, or semi-monthly
- Federal and state payroll tax filings prepared and submitted by CPAs and Enrolled Agents, not automated software alone
- Year-end W-2 and 1099 preparation and distribution
- Garnishments, benefits deductions, and PTO tracking handled without extra spreadsheets on your end

Owners in construction and restaurants tell us the same thing: they don't want to learn payroll software, they want it handled correctly and explained plainly when a question comes up.

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## Compliance and filings handled for you

Payroll tax mistakes are expensive. A missed federal deposit deadline, an incorrect Utah withholding filing, or a late Department of Workforce Services report can trigger penalties that compound quickly. Kinexus manages federal payroll tax deposits and Form 941 filings, Utah state withholding and unemployment insurance reporting, and local filing requirements specific to Washington County businesses.

Restaurant operators face additional exposure around tip reporting and FICA tip credits. Construction companies juggle prevailing wage requirements on public jobs and worker classification questions between employees and subcontractors. Medical practices manage multi-provider payroll with varying compensation models. Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, and Andrew (Andy) James Stewart, EA, work directly with the IRS and Utah State Tax Commission on your behalf when a notice does arrive, so a filing question never becomes your problem to solve alone.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: payroll-financial-dashboard.jpg | alt: "Small business owner reviewing financial reports on a laptop with an advisor" | query: "business owner reviewing financial reports laptop" -->
## Payroll that connects to your bigger financial picture

Payroll run in isolation tells you almost nothing. Payroll run alongside your bookkeeping and outsourced accounting tells you exactly what labor is costing you against revenue, job, or location, in real time.

Kinexus builds payroll data directly into the financial reporting your CPA already reviews. That means labor cost percentages show up in your monthly financials without a separate reconciliation step, and a payroll change flows into your budget the same week it happens. RJ Mathews, CPA, and the business management services team use that connected data to flag labor cost trends before they erode margin, whether you're staffing a second restaurant location or scaling a service firm past ten employees. Payroll stops being a standalone chore and becomes another input your CPA is already watching.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Industry-specific payroll challenges we solve

### Construction and Trades
icon: Hammer

Crew-based pay, prevailing wage jobs, and the constant question of employee versus 1099 subcontractor create real audit exposure. Kinexus helps classify workers correctly and keeps job-cost payroll data tied to your WIP schedules.

### Restaurants and Food Service
icon: Receipt

Tipped wages, shift differentials, and high turnover mean payroll changes weekly, sometimes daily. We handle tip credit calculations and multi-location staffing so a manager change at one restaurant doesn't create a filing error at another.

### Medical Practices
icon: Stethoscope

Physicians, associates, and hygienists often sit on different compensation structures within the same practice. Kinexus manages varied pay schedules, benefits deductions, and bonus structures without slowing down your front office.

### Service-Based Businesses
icon: Briefcase

Consultants, agencies, and staffing firms scaling past a handful of employees need payroll that keeps pace with hiring. We set up new team members fast and keep multi-state or remote-worker filings straight as you grow.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: secure-digital-payroll-portal.jpg | alt: "Business owner accessing a secure digital payroll portal on a tablet" | query: "person using tablet secure digital portal" -->
## A modern, secure payroll experience

Onboarding a new hire shouldn't mean printing forms, scanning them, and emailing PDFs back and forth. Kinexus runs payroll through a secure digital portal where employees complete their own onboarding paperwork, update direct deposit details, and access pay stubs without a phone call to your office.

On your end, approving a payroll run, reviewing a report, or signing a filing takes minutes from a phone or laptop. Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, and Morgan Nethercott, CPA, oversee the same digital process used across bookkeeping and outsourced accounting engagements, so your payroll data lives in one secure system instead of scattered spreadsheets and email threads.

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: st-george-business-owner-handshake.jpg | alt: "St. George business owner shaking hands with a CPA advisor" | query: "business owner handshake advisor office" -->
## Get payroll off your plate this pay period

If you're re-keying hours from a time clock, chasing a missed filing deadline, or fielding employee questions your software can't answer, it's time to hand payroll to people who also know your books and your tax return. Schedule a consultation with Kinexus CPAs & Advisors and see what payroll looks like when a CPA is actually watching it.

### Business management services
URL: /what-we-do/business-management-services

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: cfo-advisor-reviewing-financials.jpg | alt: "CPA and business owner reviewing financial reports at a desk" | query: "CFO advisor meeting business owner office" -->
## A CFO-level partner for growing businesses

Bookkeeping tells you what happened last month. A CFO-level advisor tells you what to do next. Kinexus Business Management Services translate financial statements into decisions: when to hire, when to buy equipment, when to raise prices, and when to hold cash instead of spending it.

Most bookkeeping shops and directory-listed providers around St. George stop at monthly reconciliations. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, built this service for owners who need more than a general ledger: a strategist who understands construction job costing, restaurant food and labor margins, or a medical practice's payer mix.

This is advisory work led by CPAs with master's-level accounting training, delivered on a schedule that matches how fast your business actually moves.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: kpi-dashboard-review-meeting.jpg | alt: "Business owner and advisor reviewing KPI dashboard on laptop screen" | query: "financial dashboard review business meeting" -->
## What our business management services include

Business Management Services cover the ground between bookkeeping and true financial strategy. It's built for owners who want a clear read on where the business stands and a plan for where it's headed next.

- Cash flow forecasting so you know what's coming before it hits your account
- KPI reporting and dashboards tailored to your industry's real performance drivers
- Budgeting and variance analysis that flags problems before they compound
- Quarterly financial strategy sessions with a CPA, not a generic account manager
- Entity structuring guidance for tax efficiency and liability protection, detailed further on our [entity structuring page](/services/entity-structuring)
- Operations efficiency consulting drawing on our team's background in operations management, covered in depth under [operations efficiency consulting](/services/operations-efficiency-consulting)

Each engagement is scoped to the business, not sold as a fixed package. A single-location restaurant needs different reporting than a contractor running three active job sites.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: contractor-real-estate-investor-planning.jpg | alt: "Contractor and advisor reviewing multi-entity business structure documents" | query: "contractor real estate investor financial planning" -->
## Built for growing and multi-entity businesses

Growth creates complexity fast. A contractor bidding bigger jobs, a real estate investor adding a third rental LLC, a consultant spinning off a second brand: each of these moves changes how the business should be structured and reported.

Our team, including Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, works with entrepreneurs and investors who are past the single-entity stage and need someone tracking consolidated performance across entities, not just filing separate returns for each one.

That means holding companies, management fees between related entities, and inter-entity loans get structured correctly from the start, with guidance detailed on our [entity structuring services page](/services/entity-structuring). Multi-entity businesses that skip this step usually pay for it later in cleanup costs and missed deductions.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: quarterly-strategy-session-office.jpg | alt: "Advisor and owner in quarterly strategy meeting with financial charts" | query: "quarterly business strategy meeting office" -->
## Proactive strategy, not year-end surprises

A lot of firms show up in March, prepare a return, and disappear until next year. That model works fine for simple returns. It fails growing businesses, where a decision made in June, a new hire, a lease, an equipment purchase, changes what April looks like.

Business Management Services run on a year-round rhythm: regular check-ins, updated forecasts, and a standing conversation about what's changing in the business. It pairs directly with our [advanced tax planning](/services/advanced-tax-planning) work for owners in higher income brackets, so tax strategy and operational strategy move together instead of getting reconciled after the fact.

The result is fewer surprises at tax time and more decisions made with real numbers instead of a gut check.

### Business tax
URL: /what-we-do/business-tax

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Business tax planning built for St. George's growing companies

Running a construction company, a restaurant, a medical practice, or a service business in Washington County means the tax code treats you differently depending on what you do and how you're structured. A once-a-year meeting with your CPA in March doesn't catch the deductions available to a growing S-corp, the depreciation options on new equipment, or the quarterly estimated payments that keep the IRS off your back. Kinexus CPAs & Advisors treats business tax as a year-round conversation, not a spring deadline. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, leads tax strategy for clients across construction, restaurants, real estate, and healthcare, building plans around entity type, growth stage, and the rules specific to each industry rather than a generic checklist. St. George business owners get a team that tracks tax law changes as they happen and applies them before the deadline, not after.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: quarterly-tax-strategy-session.jpg | alt: "CPA and business owner discussing quarterly tax strategy at a desk" | query: "accountant client meeting discussing documents" -->
## Proactive tax strategy versus once-a-year filing

Reactive tax prep looks backward: gather receipts, hand them to a preparer, hope for the best. Proactive planning looks forward. Shawn Gubler holds the Certified Tax Coach (CTC) designation, a credential built specifically around advanced strategy for high-income business owners, and it shapes how Kinexus approaches every engagement. Instead of a single filing appointment, clients get quarterly strategy sessions that revisit income projections, entity elections, retirement contributions, and deduction timing while there's still time to act. A contractor closing a strong third quarter can adjust equipment purchases before December 31. A restaurant owner expanding to a second location can restructure before the new entity opens, not after. That's the difference between a CPA who files your return and one who helps decide what the return should say. Business owners who wait until January to think about taxes have already missed most of their options for the year.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Tax solutions tailored to your industry

Tax strategy that works for a dental practice rarely works for a general contractor. Kinexus builds plans around the rules that actually apply to your business, not a template pulled off the shelf.

### Construction
icon: Hammer

Job costing, equipment depreciation, and percentage-of-completion accounting all affect what a contractor owes and when. We plan around WIP schedules and Section 179 elections so tax timing matches cash flow instead of the calendar.

### Restaurants
icon: Coins

Tip credit calculations, multi-location payroll tax, and equipment upgrades shift a restaurant's tax picture fast. We structure entities and time major purchases around the margins restaurant operators actually work with.

### Real Estate
icon: Home

Cost segregation studies, 1031 exchanges, and passive activity rules can move a rental portfolio's tax bill by tens of thousands of dollars. We map out the tax consequences of a sale or acquisition before you sign anything.

### Medical Professionals
icon: Stethoscope

Physicians and dentists face high effective tax rates without the right entity structure and retirement plan design. We build strategy around practice ownership, equipment purchases, and multi-provider partnerships.

### Service-Based Businesses
icon: Briefcase

Consultants, agencies, and staffing firms scale fast and often outgrow their entity structure within a year or two. We revisit S-corp elections, owner compensation, and deduction strategy as revenue climbs.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: entity-structuring-meeting.jpg | alt: "CPA explaining entity structure diagram to a small business owner" | query: "business consultant explaining documents office" -->
## Entity structuring and multi-entity tax strategy

Growing past a single LLC often means growing into a mess: multiple businesses, real estate held personally, no holding company, and a tax bill that reflects the disorganization. Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, works with business owners on entity structuring that separates operating risk from real estate and investment assets, sets up holding companies where they make sense, and coordinates tax treatment across related entities. This matters most for contractors who own equipment through a separate entity, medical practices splitting the practice from the real estate, and entrepreneurs running two or three ventures under one roof. The right structure isn't a one-time decision. As revenue grows, entities get acquired, or ownership changes, the structure that worked at $500,000 in revenue may start costing money at $2 million.

An IRS letter shows up in the mail and the first instinct is panic. That's normal. It's also unnecessary when you have someone who has handled this before standing next to you.

If you're staring at a notice right now, take a breath. We've been here before, and there's a process for exactly this situation.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: cpa-reviewing-audit-documents.jpg | alt: "CPA reviewing tax documents and IRS notice with client" | query: "accountant reviewing paperwork office" -->
## What our audit protection service includes

Audit protection at Kinexus means we stand between you and the IRS or Utah State Tax Commission, not just behind you offering advice from a distance. Enrollment covers:

- Reviewing and responding to IRS or state notices within required deadlines, so nothing lapses into a bigger problem
- Preparing and organizing supporting documentation, from mileage logs to job costing records to medical practice billing files
- Direct correspondence and negotiation with the examining agent on your behalf
- Attending audit meetings and interviews in your place, whenever the case allows for representative-only appearances
- Coordinating with your existing tax and bookkeeping records at Kinexus, so there's no scramble to reconstruct a year's worth of transactions
- Ongoing status updates in plain language, not IRS jargon

The goal is simple: you keep running your business while someone with the right credential handles the agency.

## Enrolled Agent representation backed by year-round tax strategy

Not every accounting firm can sit across the table from an IRS agent on your behalf. That authority belongs to Enrolled Agents, CPAs, and attorneys. At Kinexus, Andy Stewart, EA, and Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, carry that federal designation specifically, which means they can represent you before the IRS at any administrative level without you in the room.

Representation is only half the story, though. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, leads a planning approach built around reducing audit exposure before a notice ever arrives: clean entity structuring, documented job costing, consistent bookkeeping, and defensible deduction positions. Clients enrolled in ongoing tax planning through Kinexus walk into an audit with records that already hold up, because they were built that way from the start, not assembled the week the letter arrived.

## Industry-specific audit support for the businesses we know best

Audit triggers look different depending on what you do for a living, and generic documentation requests rarely fit the way your business actually operates. Kinexus builds audit defense around the industries served in the firm's day-to-day work.

### Construction
icon: Hammer

### Restaurants

### Real Estate Investors
icon: Building

icon: Stethoscope

<!-- block: process-steps | variant: vertical -->
## What to do if you've received an audit notice

The first 48 hours after an audit letter arrives matter more than most people realize. Here's the short version of what to do, and what not to do.

### Don't ignore the deadline
IRS and Utah state notices include a response window, usually 30 days. Missing it can escalate the matter or eliminate options you'd otherwise have.

### Don't respond alone
Every statement you make to an examiner becomes part of the record. Route communication through a representative who knows what the agent is actually asking for.

### Gather what you already have
Pull tax returns, bank statements, and any records referenced in the notice. Don't recreate anything or guess at figures.

### Call before you reply
Bring the notice to Kinexus before sending anything back to the IRS. We'll review the specific issue, whether it's a correspondence audit, a document request, or a full examination, and outline next steps within your first conversation.

### Enroll in ongoing representation
Once we're engaged, all further correspondence with the IRS or state agency goes through our office, not yours.

## Get audit protection before you need it

Audit protection works best as a standing part of your tax plan, not a phone call made in a panic. Whether you want to enroll ahead of time or you're holding a notice right now, the next step is the same conversation with someone who can act on it immediately.

Schedule a consultation with Kinexus CPAs & Advisors and talk through where you stand, what's at risk, and what representation looks like for your specific situation.

## Start your business on solid financial ground

Starting a business means dozens of decisions before you've earned your first dollar: entity type, EIN, bank accounts, bookkeeping software, tax elections, licensing. Get one wrong and you're paying for it later in penalties, missed deductions, or a structure that costs you thousands as you grow.

Most accountants show up once a year, in March, with a shoebox of receipts to sort through. Kinexus works differently. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and the team build your financial foundation from the day you form your entity, not after your first tax return is due. The accounting system, tax structure, and compliance calendar get set up correctly the first time, so you spend your early months building the business instead of untangling paperwork.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: startup-checklist-review.jpg | alt: "Entrepreneur reviewing a business startup checklist with an advisor" | query: "entrepreneur reviewing startup checklist advisor" -->
## Key startup decisions handled from day one

New business owners face a stack of foundational decisions in the first 90 days. Here's what we help you sort through before they turn into costly mistakes:

- Entity selection: LLC, S-corp, C-corp, partnership, or sole proprietorship, matched to your liability exposure and tax goals
- EIN and state registration: getting your business properly registered with the IRS and the Utah Division of Corporations
- Accounting system setup: choosing and configuring software, such as QuickBooks Online, that scales as revenue grows
- Tax election strategy: timing an S-corp election, choosing a fiscal year, and setting up estimated payments correctly from the start
- Initial compliance requirements: business licenses, sales tax registration, payroll setup, and recordkeeping standards that hold up under a lender or IRS review

Miss one of these early, and you often can't fix it retroactively. That's why the sequence matters as much as the individual decisions.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: entity-structure-planning-meeting.jpg | alt: "CPA and business owner discussing entity structure options at a desk" | query: "business owners reviewing entity structure documents" -->
## Entity structuring built for growth, not just launch

The entity that makes sense at launch isn't always the entity that makes sense at $2 million in revenue. Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, and RJ Mathews, CPA, work with entrepreneurs to structure entities for where the business is headed, not where it started.

A single-member LLC might be the right call in year one. Once you're hiring employees, bringing on partners, or holding real estate alongside operations, that structure often needs to change. We look at multi-entity setups, holding companies, and the timing of S-corp elections as revenue climbs, and we revisit the structure at each stage instead of leaving it set on autopilot. Full entity structuring support is available through our [entity structuring service](/services/entity-structuring).

Most first-time owners start with a spreadsheet or a shoebox, and there's nothing wrong with that in month one. The problem shows up in month twelve, when a bank wants financials for a loan, or an investor asks for a P&L, and none of it reconciles.

Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, and Morgan Nethercott, CPA, help new business owners set up a bookkeeping system built to scale: transactions categorized correctly, accounts reconciled monthly, and reports ready to hand a lender or investor without a scramble. Once the foundation is in place, it connects directly into our ongoing [bookkeeping](/what-we-do/bookkeeping) and [outsourced accounting](/what-we-do/outsourced-accounting) services, so you're not rebuilding your books a year in.

### IRS representation and tax resolution
URL: /services/irs-representation-tax-resolution

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Facing an IRS notice or audit does not mean facing it alone

An IRS letter shows up in the mailbox and the rest of the day disappears. Maybe it's an audit notice, a demand for returns you never filed, or a notice that a lien is about to hit your property. The first instinct is panic. The second is not knowing who to call.

Kinexus CPAs & Advisors handles these situations year-round, not just during tax season. Licensed enrolled agents on our team step in as your authorized representative, communicate directly with the IRS on your behalf, and build a resolution plan based on your actual case file rather than guesswork. You don't need to understand tax code to get through this. You need someone who already does, sitting across the table from you in St. George, ready to make the calls the IRS won't return when you place them yourself.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: enrolled-agent-irs-meeting.jpg | alt: "Enrolled agent reviewing IRS correspondence with a client" | query: "tax advisor client meeting documents" -->
## How our Enrolled Agent credential works in your favor

Not every accountant can legally speak to the IRS on your behalf. An Enrolled Agent, or EA, holds a federal license granting unlimited rights of representation before the IRS, covering audits, collections, and appeals, in any state, for any tax matter. It's a credential earned through IRS examination or prior IRS service, not a title anyone can claim.

Andy Stewart, EA, and Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, hold this license at Kinexus. That means when the IRS wants documentation, a response, or a negotiation, they talk to us directly instead of routing everything back through you. A bookkeeper can help you organize paperwork. An EA can sign a power of attorney, argue your case, and negotiate terms with an IRS agent on the phone. That distinction matters the moment a case gets contested.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## IRS problems we resolve

### Audit Representation
icon: ShieldCheck

We manage correspondence and in-person audits from notice to resolution, reviewing your IRS file, preparing documentation, and speaking to the agent so you don't have to explain your own return under pressure.

### Unfiled Tax Returns
icon: FileText

Missed a year, or several? We reconstruct records, file the returns needed to bring you current, and negotiate with the IRS to limit penalties tied to the gap.

### Back Taxes & Balances Owed
icon: DollarSign

We assess what's actually owed, correct IRS errors when they exist, and structure a realistic path to resolve the balance without draining your business or household.

### Wage Garnishment & Lien Release
icon: Scale

When the IRS moves to garnish wages or file a lien, timing matters. We intervene directly with the IRS to negotiate release or modification before it disrupts payroll or a property sale.

### Penalty Abatement
icon: FileCheck

Penalties for late filing or late payment can often be reduced or removed for reasonable cause. We build the case and submit the request on your behalf.

### Installment Agreements
icon: Calendar

We negotiate payment terms with the IRS that fit your actual cash flow, whether that's a standard installment plan or a more structured settlement option.

<!-- block: process-steps | variant: horizontal -->
## What happens after you contact us

### We pull and review your IRS file
Before we respond to anything, we request a full transcript of your account directly from the IRS. This shows us exactly what they have on record, what deadlines are real, and what options are actually available in your case.

### We build a strategy session around your numbers
You meet with an enrolled agent or CPA to walk through the findings, your goals, and the realistic paths forward, whether that's abatement, an installment agreement, or audit defense.

### We represent you directly with the IRS
Once you sign a power of attorney, we become your point of contact. Calls, letters, and negotiations run through our office in St. George, not yours.

Shawn Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, RJ Mathews, CPA, Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, and Morgan Nethercott, CPA, bring that industry depth across construction, restaurants, real estate, medical practices, and service-based businesses. ### Advanced tax planning for high income owners
URL: /services/advanced-tax-planning

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: high-income-tax-planning-review.jpg | alt: "CPA reviewing tax strategy documents with a business owner" | query: "accountant client meeting tax documents" -->
## Why high income business owners need more than tax prep

Most CPA firms in St. George file your return once a year, tell you the damage, and see you again in twelve months. By the time you're sitting across the table in March, the tax year is closed. There's nothing left to plan around, only numbers left to report.

High income owners don't have that luxury. A construction company clearing seven figures, a physician with a growing practice, a real estate investor closing three properties a year: these situations generate tax consequences all year long, not just at filing time. Reactive prep catches what already happened. Advanced planning changes what happens next.

Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, leads Kinexus's advanced planning work with a Certified Tax Coach credential most local firms don't carry. Combined with a Master of Accountancy-level bench that includes Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc and RJ Mathews, CPA, the firm builds strategy around your entities and income, not a generic checklist applied to every client in St. George.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->
## Advanced strategies built for growing and multi-entity businesses

Owners with more than one entity, multiple properties, or a mix of active and passive income face decisions a standard 1040 preparer isn't trained to catch. Kinexus builds strategy around the structure you actually have.

### Entity structuring and restructuring
icon: Building2

S-corp elections, multi-entity holding structures, and management company setups can shift how much of your income is subject to self-employment tax. We review your entity map at least annually as revenue and holdings change.

### Income shifting and timing strategies
icon: TrendingUp

Moving income and deductions between years, entities, or family members, done correctly and documented, can lower your effective rate without triggering IRS scrutiny.

### Retirement and deferred compensation planning
icon: PiggyBank

Defined benefit plans, cash balance plans, and solo 401(k) strategies let high-earning owners defer six figures in some years while building long-term wealth outside the business.

### Multi-entity coordination
icon: FileText

When a single owner runs a construction company, a real estate holding entity, and a management company, the tax return for one affects the others. MAcc-level review catches interactions a generalist misses.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: certified-tax-coach-planning-session.jpg | alt: "Certified tax coach explaining a tax strategy plan to a client" | query: "financial advisor explaining strategy document" -->
## Certified Tax Coach-level planning for high-income owners

The Certified Tax Coach designation Shawn Gubler holds requires ongoing training in strategies most CPAs never study: cost segregation studies, advanced entity elections, and timing strategies that hold up under IRS review because they're built on real transactions and real documentation.

Cost segregation, for example, reclassifies parts of a commercial or rental property into shorter depreciation schedules, front-loading deductions in years when you need them most. Entity elections like S-corp status or partnership restructuring can reduce self-employment tax exposure by tens of thousands of dollars a year for the right owner. Timing strategies around equipment purchases, retirement contributions, and income recognition move tax liability to the year where it costs you the least.

None of this is aggressive for the sake of aggressive. It's compliant, documented, and specific to owners in the higher brackets, which is exactly why a once-a-year filing firm rarely gets there. They don't have the bandwidth, and often not the credential, to build it.

A generic tax plan misses the details that actually move the needle in your industry. Kinexus builds planning around how your business actually operates.

### Contractors and construction owners
icon: Hammer

Job costing, retainage timing, and equipment depreciation decisions all carry tax weight. Planning around WIP schedules and percentage-of-completion accounting keeps your tax position aligned with how revenue actually recognizes.

### Medical professionals
icon: Stethoscope

Practice owners face entity decisions, equipment purchases, and retirement plan design questions that differ from a typical small business. We plan around practice growth, not just this year's income.

### Real estate investors
icon: Home

Cost segregation, 1031 exchanges, and passive activity rules shape what an investor owes each year. Planning ahead of a sale or acquisition, not after closing, is what protects the deduction.

### Service-based businesses
icon: Briefcase

Consultants, agencies, coaches, and staffing firms often carry uneven income and multiple contractor relationships. Entity structure and quarterly estimates get built around that variability.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: irs-audit-representation-meeting.jpg | alt: "Tax professional reviewing an IRS notice with a client at a desk" | query: "accountant reviewing IRS notice letter" -->
## Protection and support if the IRS comes calling

Higher income draws more attention. Owners in the top brackets, especially those using entity structures and cost segregation, see more audit scrutiny than the average filer. That's not a reason to avoid the strategy. It's a reason to have representation built into the relationship from the start.

Kinexus's audit protection service puts Enrolled Agents Andrew Stewart, EA, and Peter Williams, EA, MAcc, in your corner if the IRS sends a notice, a letter, or opens an audit. Because they're already familiar with your entity structure and planning history, there's no scramble to explain three years of decisions to someone meeting your file for the first time.

### Entity structuring for growing businesses
URL: /services/entity-structuring

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: business-growth-planning-meeting.jpg | alt: "Business owner and advisor reviewing entity paperwork at a desk" | query: "business owner advisor reviewing documents" -->
## When your current structure stops serving your growth

Most entity decisions get made once, in the excitement of opening day, and then never get revisited. That works fine until it doesn't. A construction company that started as a single-member LLC and now runs three crews and $2 million in annual revenue faces different liability exposure and tax brackets than the day it formed. A medical practice adding a second physician-owner needs a structure that handles distributions, buy-in, and liability differently than a solo practitioner setup.

Certain triggers should prompt a structure review: crossing into a new tax bracket, bringing on a business partner, acquiring rental property or a second location, or separating operations from real estate holdings. If any of these sound familiar, your entity paperwork may be costing you money or exposing you to risk it was never built to handle.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: llc-scorp-comparison-review.jpg | alt: "CPA pointing to entity comparison chart during client meeting" | query: "accountant explaining chart client" -->
## Choosing between LLCs, S-corps, and multi-entity setups

An LLC taxed as a sole proprietorship or partnership is simple to maintain but leaves self-employment tax exposure on your full share of profit. Elect S-corp treatment once profits justify it, and you can split income between salary and distributions, often reducing that tax bite. An S-corp comes with payroll requirements, reasonable-compensation rules, and stricter ownership limits that don't fit every business.

For owners running more than one line of business, or holding real estate alongside operations, a single entity often isn't the right answer at all. The choice isn't LLC versus S-corp in isolation. It's which combination protects your assets, minimizes your combined tax bill, and still lets you run the business without unnecessary complexity.

Questions worth answering before you file anything:

- Self-employment tax exposure under a default LLC
- Payroll and reasonable-compensation requirements once an S-corp election makes sense
- Liability separation between operating entities and asset-holding entities
- State filing, franchise tax, and registered agent differences across structures

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: holding-company-real-estate-structure.jpg | alt: "Real estate investor and accountant discussing property portfolio structure" | query: "real estate investor accountant meeting" -->
## Structuring for multiple entities, holding companies, and real estate

Owners running more than one business, or layering real estate into their holdings, need structuring that goes beyond a single LLC filing. Shawn Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and Chase Gubler, CPA, MAcc, work through multi-entity structures where an operating company handles day-to-day business and a separate holding company owns the real estate, equipment, or intellectual property leased back to it.

This separation matters for two reasons: liability and tax. If a slip-and-fall claim hits your restaurant's operating entity, the building and equipment sitting in a separate holding LLC stay protected. On the tax side, a holding company structure can create rental deductions, depreciation planning, and cleaner books when it's time to sell one piece of the business without unwinding the whole thing.

Real estate investors with multiple properties face a related question: one LLC per property, a series LLC, or a portfolio-level entity. The right answer depends on financing needs, the number of properties, and how actively you're acquiring.

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## How entity structure connects to your tax strategy

Entity structure isn't a form you file once and forget. It's one lever in a tax plan that gets reviewed every year, not just when a return is due. Shawn Gubler holds the Certified Tax Coach (CTC) credential specifically because tax planning built around a client's structure, timing, and elections produces bigger savings than year-end scrambling ever will.

An S-corp election that made sense at $80,000 in profit may cost you money at $400,000, once payroll taxes, retirement plan limits, and qualified business income deductions shift the math. A multi-entity setup built for liability protection five years ago might now be creating unnecessary complexity if one of those entities sits dormant.

Entity structure gets reviewed as part of ongoing tax planning, not as a stand-alone project. That means catching the moment your structure needs an update before it shows up as a bigger tax bill next April.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Built for St. George's contractors, medical practices, and service businesses

Generic entity advice misses the details that matter most inside specific industries. Here's what that looks like in practice.

### Contractors and Construction Businesses
icon: Hammer

Joint ventures between contractors bidding larger jobs need an entity layer that divides liability and profit without complicating each partner's existing company. Structuring gets built alongside WIP schedule and percentage-of-completion reporting so the entity and the accounting method work together.

### Medical and Dental Practices
icon: Stethoscope

Adding a second physician-owner, opening a satellite location, or separating the practice from the building it operates in each call for a different approach than a solo practitioner uses. Practice groups get structured to handle buy-in, distributions, and liability separately from real estate holdings.

### Service-Based Businesses
icon: Briefcase

Consultants, agencies, and staffing firms scaling past a founder-only operation often outgrow a simple LLC once contractors, multiple owners, or a second revenue line enter the picture. Structuring here targets the growth stage a business is actually in, not a generic startup template.

## How we guide you through a structure change

### Financial and risk review
The process starts with a review of your current entity, tax returns, and liability exposure to identify what's actually costing you money or leaving you exposed.

### Structure recommendation
Next comes a recommendation for the entity or multi-entity combination that fits your revenue, ownership, and asset-protection needs, with the tax impact modeled out in plain numbers.

### Coordination with legal counsel
Entity formation and operating agreements are legal work. Coordination happens directly with your attorney, or a referral if you need one, so the paperwork matches the tax strategy.

### Implementation and ongoing monitoring
Once the new structure is filed, your books, payroll, and tax elections get updated accordingly, then revisited during annual tax planning as your business changes.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: back-office-warning-signs.jpg | alt: "Overwhelmed small business owner surrounded by paperwork at desk" | query: "stressed business owner paperwork desk" -->
## Signs your back office is holding your business back

Back office drag rarely announces itself. It shows up as a gut feeling that something's off, or a pile of small frustrations that add up to real cost.

- You're closing the books two or three weeks late every month, so decisions get made on stale numbers
- Bookkeeping, payroll, and invoicing live in three different systems that don't talk to each other
- The owner still approves every invoice, reconciles every account, or runs payroll personally
- Nobody can tell you gross margin by job, project, or location without a week of digging
- You've hired administrative help, but tasks still fall through the cracks
- Financial reporting tells you what happened last quarter, not what's happening now

If two or more of these sound familiar, the problem usually isn't effort. It's structure.

## Job costing and work in progress reporting that keeps projects profitable

A job that looks profitable on paper can bleed cash for months before anyone notices. Most off-the-shelf bookkeeping setups track expenses company-wide, not by project phase, so a contractor can't tell which job is actually making money until it's too late to adjust the bid or the crew schedule.

We build job costing systems that break down labor, materials, subcontractor invoices, and overhead by job and phase, so profitability shows up in real time instead of at tax time. Our [WIP schedules](/industries/construction/wip-schedules-percentage-completion) follow percentage-of-completion methods your bonding agent and lender already expect, updated on a schedule you can actually use when bidding the next job.

Retainage sitting on the balance sheet is its own cash flow problem. We help you [plan around it](/retainage-is-holding-your-cash-hostage-heres-how-to-plan-around-it) instead of discovering the gap when payroll is due.

## Accounting built for the realities of running a restaurant

Thin margins, cash drawers that need reconciling every night, and a staff roster that turns over every few months: restaurant accounting has almost nothing in common with bookkeeping for a retail shop or a law office. Prime cost has to be tracked weekly, not quarterly, or a bad week in food cost eats the whole month's profit. Kinexus CPAs & Advisors works with restaurant and food & beverage operators across St. George and Washington County, from single-location cafes to multi-unit groups managing tourist traffic near Zion National Park and Sand Hollow. <!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: startup-founder-paperwork-stress.jpg | alt: "Small business owner sorting through financial paperwork at a desk" | query: "stressed entrepreneur reviewing paperwork" -->
## Where new businesses run into trouble without the right foundation

Most startup accounting problems trace back to decisions made in the first six months. The same patterns show up across contractors, restaurant operators, and service-based founders launching new companies in southern Utah:

- Choosing an LLC, S-corp, or sole proprietorship without understanding the tax tradeoffs
- Mixing personal and business funds in one bank account
- Missing an S-corp or entity election that had a hard filing deadline
- Running the business with no real-time view of cash flow or margin
- Doing bookkeeping in spreadsheets that don't reconcile once tax season arrives

None of this means the business is failing. It means the founder was busy building something, which is exactly why the accounting and tax foundation needs to be right before it costs real money to fix.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->
## Business foundation services to start strong

Some early decisions are hard to unwind once they're made. Entity type, tax elections, and how the books get set up on day one all fall into that category, so getting them right the first time matters more than most founders realize.

### Entity structuring
icon: Scale

LLC, S-corp, partnership, or sole proprietorship each carry different tax and liability outcomes. We help founders pick the structure that fits how the business actually operates, not a generic default.

### EIN and business registration
icon: FileCheck

Federal EIN, state registration, and local licensing in Washington County get handled correctly the first time, so a missed filing doesn't surface as a penalty later.

### Chart of accounts setup
icon: ClipboardCheck

A chart of accounts built for the business's actual revenue streams and cost structure, so the numbers mean something from the first transaction forward.

### Initial tax elections
icon: FileText

S-corp elections, accounting method choices, and other early filings have real deadlines. Missing one can mean waiting a full year to fix it.

Shawn T. Gubler holds the Certified Tax Coach (CTC) credential alongside his CPA and MAcc, and it shows up in how the firm approaches business and personal tax together. ## A CPA partner built for real estate investors and operators

Kinexus CPAs & Advisors works out of St. George, Utah with rental property owners, real estate investors, agents, developers, and property management companies across Washington County and beyond. Real estate wealth is built and protected in the decisions made all year long, not in a single spring filing appointment.

That's where most tax relationships fall short. One call in April, a return assembled from a folder of receipts, and silence until next January. Kinexus runs differently. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, and the team meet with real estate clients throughout the year to plan acquisitions, structure entities, and review depreciation schedules before decisions get locked in. Whether you hold three rental doors or manage a portfolio spread across multiple LLCs, the goal stays the same: fewer surprises at tax time and a clear line of sight into your cash flow.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: real-estate-portfolio-review.jpg | alt: "Real estate investor reviewing rental property documents at a desk" | query: "real estate investor reviewing property documents" -->
## Accounting challenges unique to real estate

Real estate accounting rarely stays simple past the second property. Each acquisition raises a new question: hold it in an existing LLC, form a new entity, or roll it into a series structure? Get the entity setup wrong and you end up with commingled liability, messier books, and a harder conversation with your lender.

Depreciation adds another layer. Rental property depreciation, cost segregation opportunities, and bonus depreciation rules shift the math on every property differently, and missing a component-level breakdown can leave real deductions unclaimed. Add passive activity loss limitations, the real estate professional status test, and the timing rules around 1031 exchanges, and it's easy to see why generic tax prep leaves money on the table.

Kinexus works through these details before the deal closes, not after the return is filed. That includes mapping out how a 1031 exchange affects your basis, whether a cost segregation study makes sense for a recent purchase, and how passive activity rules apply to your specific mix of properties and involvement.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Services tailored to real estate portfolios

### Bookkeeping & Outsourced Accounting
icon: Calculator

Property-level bookkeeping that separates income and expenses by unit, entity, or project. Monthly reconciliations, expense categorization, and reporting built so you can see which properties are actually performing. [See outsourced accounting](/what-we-do/outsourced-accounting)

### Business Tax Planning & Preparation
icon: FileText

Year-round tax planning for LLCs, partnerships, and S corps holding rental or investment property, with depreciation strategy and entity-level filings handled together instead of as an afterthought. [Explore business tax services](/what-we-do/business-tax)

### Business Management Services
icon: ChartLine

CFO-level insight for investors scaling past a handful of properties: cash flow forecasting for acquisitions, investor reporting packages, and multi-entity financial statements that hold up with lenders and partners. [Learn about business management services](/what-we-do/business-management-services)

### Entity Structuring & Advanced Tax Planning
icon: Building2

Guidance on how to hold each property, when to split entities, and how 1031 exchanges, cost segregation, and depreciation strategy fit together across a growing portfolio. [Review entity structuring](/services/entity-structuring)

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## Proactive tax strategy for property owners and investors

Shawn T. Gubler holds the Certified Tax Coach (CTC) designation, a credential built specifically around advanced, forward-looking tax planning rather than compliance-only preparation. That distinction matters for real estate clients, where the biggest savings usually come from decisions made months before a return is ever filed.

Depreciation strategy is a good example. A cost segregation study on a recently acquired rental or commercial property can accelerate deductions into the years you need them most, but only if it's planned before year-end, not discovered during filing season. The same goes for 1031 exchanges: the identification and closing windows are unforgiving, and the tax outcome depends on decisions made well before the exchange agreement is signed.

Entity structuring works the same way. Whether a new acquisition belongs in an existing LLC, a new one, or a holding company arrangement changes your liability exposure and your tax picture at the same time. Kinexus builds these conversations into regular check-ins throughout the year, so the strategy is set before the transaction closes, not reconstructed after the fact.

- Secure client portal for uploading closing statements, lease agreements, and 1099s from any device
- Digital signatures for engagement letters and tax filings, no in-person visit required
- Bank and property management software integrations that pull transactions automatically

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: dental-practice-finances-review.jpg | alt: "Dentist and accountant reviewing practice financial statements together" | query: "dentist reviewing financial documents office" -->
## Financial challenges unique to medical and dental practices

Running a practice comes with money problems your restaurant-owning neighbor down the street never has to think about. A few show up on almost every new client's desk in the first meeting:

- High personal income tax exposure from W-2 wages, K-1 practice income, or a mix of both, often pushing physicians and dentists into the top federal brackets
- Entity structuring decisions between an S-corp, PLLC, or partnership that affect self-employment tax, liability, and how profits get paid out to owners
- Equipment financing for imaging machines, dental chairs, or surgical tools that needs to be planned around depreciation rules, not just monthly payments
- Payroll complexity across hygienists, nurses, front-office staff, and associate providers, each with different pay structures and benefit elections
- Cash flow gaps created by insurance reimbursement timelines that can run 30, 60, or 90 days behind the date of service

Most of these problems don't get solved by a bookkeeper who logs in once a quarter. They get solved by an accounting team that understands practice economics year-round.

## Proactive tax planning for high-income healthcare providers

Most tax preparers show up in March, run the numbers on what already happened, and file the return. That approach costs high earners real money. Physicians and dentists routinely leave deductions, retirement contributions, and entity elections on the table simply because nobody looked at their situation before December 31.

Shawn T. Gubler's Certified Tax Coach (CTC) credential exists for exactly this problem. Advanced tax planning for medical professionals means reviewing entity structure for practice ownership, evaluating defined benefit and cash balance retirement plans that can shelter six figures of income, timing equipment purchases against Section 179 and bonus depreciation, and building a strategy months before filing season instead of scrambling during it. Kinexus runs this planning year-round, not as a one-time engagement, through the same [advanced tax planning](/services/advanced-tax-planning) and [entity structuring](/services/entity-structuring) work applied to other high-income clients.

## A financial partner built for consultants, agencies, coaches, and staffing firms

Consultants, marketing agencies, IT firms, staffing companies, and coaches run on a different financial model than a retail shop or a contractor. Growth often outpaces the founder's ability to track it all in a spreadsheet.

Kinexus CPAs & Advisors works with service-based businesses across St. George, Utah, who need more than a bookkeeper who logs transactions once a month. Our team, led by CPAs Shawn T. Gubler (CTC, MAcc), RJ Mathews, Chase Gubler (MAcc), and Morgan Nethercott, alongside EAs Andy Stewart and Peter Williams (MAcc), builds financial systems around how consulting, agency, coaching, and staffing businesses actually operate. <!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: agency-team-reviewing-finances.jpg | alt: "Small agency team reviewing financial reports at a shared table" | query: "agency team reviewing reports office" -->
## The financial challenges service businesses face as they scale

Service businesses hit predictable friction points as they grow past the founder's laptop and personal spreadsheet.

- Revenue that's lumpy. Retainers renew, project fees land in chunks, and staffing placements pay out on client timelines you don't control, which makes forecasting hard without a system built for irregular cash flow.
- Contractor versus employee classification. A firm mixing 1099 subcontractors with W-2 staff faces payroll tax exposure and IRS scrutiny the moment those lines blur.
- Founder-led bottlenecks. The person who built the business is often still approving invoices and tracking billable hours, which caps growth at the limit of one calendar.
- Billing-cycle cash gaps. Net-30 and net-60 client terms mean payroll and rent come due long before invoices clear, squeezing working capital right when you're hiring.

These show up in the books of agencies, consultancies, and staffing firms month after month. They're solvable with the right structure in place before they become a crisis.

### Manufacturing and distribution
URL: /who-we-serve/manufacturing-distribution

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: manufacturing-team-planning.jpg | alt: "CPA and manufacturing business owner reviewing financial reports together" | query: "manufacturing business owner meeting accountant" -->
## Financial guidance built for manufacturers and distributors

Manufacturing and distribution businesses in St. George, UT run on tight margins, seasonal demand swings, and equipment that never stops depreciating. A generalist accountant who prepares your return once a year and disappears until next April cannot keep pace with that.

Kinexus CPAs & Advisors built its practice around industries that most local firms treat as an afterthought. Shawn T. Gubler, CPA, CTC, MAcc, leads a team that studies job costing, inventory valuation, and capital equipment cycles the way manufacturers study their own production lines. Instead of a once-a-year filing relationship, you get a CPA firm that checks in throughout the year, flags cash flow gaps before they become problems, and structures your business for the next expansion, not just the next tax deadline.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: warehouse-inventory-check.jpg | alt: "Warehouse worker checking inventory boxes with a clipboard" | query: "warehouse inventory checklist worker" -->
## Challenges unique to manufacturing and distribution businesses

Manufacturing and distribution carry accounting complexities that trip up firms accustomed to simpler service businesses.

- **Inventory costing:** FIFO, LIFO, or weighted average methods change your reported margins and your tax bill. Get it wrong and you either overpay taxes or misstate profitability to your bank.
- **Supply chain cash flow gaps:** Raw materials get purchased months before finished goods sell. Without a forecast built around your production cycle, payroll and supplier payments collide with slow-paying customers.
- **Equipment and capital investment decisions:** A new CNC machine, forklift fleet, or warehouse expansion changes your depreciation schedule, loan covenants, and tax position all at once.
- **Margin pressure:** Rising material costs and freight rates squeeze distributors from both ends. Job costing that is even a few weeks stale hides which product lines are actually profitable.

Firms outside this niche often lump these numbers into generic categories that satisfy a tax return but tell you nothing about how to run the business.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Accounting and advisory services for your operation

Every service we offer ties back to how manufacturing and distribution operations actually work, from the warehouse floor to the balance sheet.

### Outsourced Accounting
icon: Building2

Full back-office support for growing operations, including multi-location consolidation, inventory account reconciliation, and monthly financials your lenders and management team can actually use. [Outsourced Accounting](/what-we-do/outsourced-accounting)

### Bookkeeping
icon: Receipt

Daily transaction classification, purchase order tracking, and vendor bill payment kept current so your cost of goods sold numbers reflect reality, not last quarter's guesswork. [Bookkeeping](/what-we-do/bookkeeping)

### Payroll
icon: Users

Multi-location and multi-shift payroll processing, including prevailing wage requirements where applicable, plus timely filings so plant and warehouse staff get paid without delay. [Payroll](/what-we-do/payroll)

### Business Tax
icon: FileText
